nodes.name: Hydrothermal Coprecipitation
nodes.procedure: The Ni²⁺ and MoO₄²⁻ ions were initially coprecipitated through a hydrothermal treatment to form the NiMo-based nanorods (i.e., NiMoO₄ crystals) with a smooth surface.
nodes.source_text: the Ni²⁺ and MoO₄²⁻ ions were initially coprecipitated through a hydrothermal treatment to form the NiMo-based nanorods (i.e., NiMoO₄ crystals) with a smooth surface

nodes.name: Moderate Reduction Calcination
nodes.procedure: After the calcination at 450 °C under H₂/Ar atmosphere, the as-designed Ni/NiO@MoO₃₋ₓ nanoarray consisting of surface Ni/NiO nanocrystals and MoO₃₋ₓ nanorods were obtained.
nodes.source_text: After the calcination at 450 °C under H₂/Ar atmosphere, the as-designed Ni/NiO@MoO₃₋ₓ nanoarray consisting of surface Ni/NiO nanocrystals and MoO₃₋ₓ nanorods were obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM shows Ni/NiO@MoO3−x nanoarray composed of cuboid nanorods on nickel foam substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) images (Figure 1b,c) clearly show that the Ni/NiO@MoO3−x nanoarray on the nickel foam substrate is composed of cuboid nanorods.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows surface of Ni/NiO@MoO3−x cuboid nanorods covered by numerous small nanoparticles of ≈20 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast with the smooth surface of the precursor nanorods, the surface of Ni/NiO@MoO3−x cuboid nanorods is covered by numerous small nanoparticles of ≈20 nm, evidenced by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 1d).

nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Figure 1e) exhibits bigger nanoparticles (≈15 nm) surrounded by smaller ones (≈6 nm) are embedded in the nanorod matrix... The lattice spacing of the large nanoparticles and small nanoparticles is 0.20 and 0.21 nm, which is ascribed to the Ni (111) and NiO (202) planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED shows diffraction spots at d-spacings 0.13 nm (Ni (220)), 0.18 nm (Ni (200)), 0.21 nm (NiO (202)) and diffraction ring from amorphous MoO3−x.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern displays a series of diffraction spots and a diffraction ring (Figure S5, Supporting Information). Three different d-spacing values of the diffraction spots are discerned to be 0.13, 0.18, and 0.21 nm, corresponding to Ni (220), Ni (200), and NiO (202) planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows lower Mo─O bond intensity at 347 and 947 cm⁻¹ for Ni/NiO@MoO3−x vs precursor, verifying amorphous MoO3−x phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra of the Ni/NiO@MoO3−x and NiMo-based precursor reveal that the Ni/NiO@MoO3−x has a lower band intensity of Mo─O bonds at 347 and 947 cm⁻¹ (Figure S6, Supporting Information), verifying a weaker Mo─O bond vibration and the amorphous phase of MoO3−x.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows homogeneous Mo and O distribution in Ni/NiO@MoO3−x nanorod matrix with uneven Ni distribution; Ni:Mo ratio 39.5:60.5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mapping images confirm that all elements are equally distributed in the NiMoO4 precursor nanorods (Figure S7, Supporting Information). Moreover, the Mo and O elements are homogeneously distributed in the composite Ni/NiO@MoO3−x, indicating that the nanorod matrix is composed of MoO3−x, whereas the Ni element is unevenly distributed (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows NiO peaks at 37.2° (021), 43.2° (202), 62.8° (220) and Ni peaks at 44.6° (111), 51.9° (200); no MoO3 peaks observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Ni/NiO@MoO3−x (Figure S8, Supporting Information) consists of five major diffraction peaks, which three peaks at 37.2°, 43.2°, and 62.8° can be indexed to the (021), (202), and (220) planes of NiO (JCPDS: 89-3080), while the rest two peaks at 44.6° and 51.9° are assigned to the Ni (111) and (200) planes (JCPDS: 70-0989).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms Ni:Mo atomic ratio consistent with EDX results (Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDX spectrum results show that Ni:Mo atomic ratio of the Ni/NiO@MoO3−x nanorods is 39.5:60.5 (Figure S9, Supporting Information), agreeing well with the inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometer (ICP-OES) results (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS of Ni/NiO@MoO3−x shows metallic Ni signal at ≈851.7 eV and Ni(II) at 854.9 eV confirming coexistence; Mo 3d shows Mo(VI) 3d5/2 at 232.6 eV, 3d3/2 at 235.7 eV and Mo(IV) at 230.6 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, three signal bands at ≈851.7 and 854.9 eV, that, respectively, derived from the metallic Ni and Ni (II) signals, were detected by the Ni 2p high-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectra (XPS) of Ni@MoO3−x and Ni/NiO@MoO3−x... Furthermore, results from Mo 3d high-resolution XPS spectra demonstrate Mo(VI) 3d5/2 at 232.6 eV, and Mo(VI) 3d3/2 at 235.7 eV... the Mo signal band at 230.6 eV of Ni/NiO@MoO3−x nanorods is aroused by the Mo (IV) state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES pre-edge at ≈8333 eV (between Ni ≈8332 eV and NiO ≈8340 eV) confirms Ni/NiO coexistence in Ni/NiO@MoO3−x; Mo K-edge negative shift confirms MoO3−x phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectrum results of Ni K-edge for the Ni/NiO@MoO3−x catalyst present a significantly different pre-edge feature centered at ≈8333 eV... Furthermore, the Mo K-edge XANES spectrum of the Ni/NiO@MoO3−x catalyst reveals a negative shift in contrast with that of NiMoO4 precursor, confirming the existence of MoO3−x phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows Ni─Ni (≈2.0 Å), Ni─O (≈2.5 Å), Mo─Ni (≈3.2 Å), Mo─O (≈2.0 Å) bonds with negative radial shifts vs standards.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fourier transforms of the extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectrum and the corresponding simulation k³-weighted spectrum at the K edges of Ni, the Ni─Ni (≈2.0 Å) and Ni─O bonds (≈2.5 Å) in the Ni/NiO@MoO3−x catalyst were detected... the Mo─Ni bond (≈3.2 Å) and the radial distance shifts of the Mo─O bond (≈2.0 Å) could be observed in the Ni/NiO@MoO3−x catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR shows characteristic O-D vibration band at ≈2500 cm⁻¹ for Ni/NiO@MoO3−x after D₂O adsorption, confirming enhanced water adsorption ability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-IR spectra of the Ni/NiO@MoO3−x and Ni@MoO3−x samples show a characteristic band at ≈2500 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the O-D vibration.
